summary: The paper adds Fortran directives for regular and reshaped array distribution on a cache-coherent NUMA multiprocessor, with affinity scheduling to run iterations where their data lives. It reports that reshaping, together with compiler optimizations of the resulting address arithmetic, can beat page-granular placement on fine-grained distributions.
why_read: It shows how a production compiler can offer data placement on shared-memory machines where OS page granularity is too coarse for some distributions.
main_contribution: Regular and reshaped data distribution directives with affinity scheduling, implemented in the SGI MIPSpro compiler, plus optimizations that reduce the cost of reshaped array addressing.
main_limitation: Reshaped arrays cannot be redistributed dynamically and carry legality restrictions and addressing overhead.
evaluation_method: measured speedup and execution time on a 128-processor Origin-2000
